alt.en: A colour photographic print of a long stone college building with battlements, tall chimneys and pinnacled towers, its walls hung with ivy, rising above a narrow, still river lined with trees. In the distance a stone bridge with a balustrade crosses the water.
alt.es: Copia fotográfica en color de un largo edificio de piedra de un colegio universitario, con almenas, chimeneas altas y torres con pináculos y muros cubiertos de hiedra, que se alza sobre un río estrecho y quieto bordeado de árboles. A lo lejos, un puente de piedra con balaustrada cruza el agua.

caption.en: Magdalen College, Oxford, from the river, in a photochrom print of the 1890s. In 1867 Bramley was a Fellow of the college and Stainer its organist, and together they made the book that holds the carol's earliest known printing.
caption.es: El Magdalen College de Oxford visto desde el río, en un fotocromo de la década de 1890. En 1867 Bramley era miembro (fellow) del colegio y Stainer su organista, y juntos hicieron el libro donde está la primera impresión conocida del villancico.

source: [Magdalen College, from the river, Oxford, England], photochrom print no. 10083, Views of the British Isles (Detroit Publishing Co. catalogue, 1905)
library: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
licenceEvidence: Library of Congress record https://www.loc.gov/item/2002708028/ (read in the Wayback Machine, capture 2025-12-06): Rights Advisory "No known restrictions on publication." Also PD by age: photochrom published between about 1890 and 1900, no maker named (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-ppmsc-08767

alt.en: A printed table headed "INDEX. First Series.", with columns for number, title, source of words, air and page, listing twenty carols from I to XX. Row XIV reads "What Child is this?", "W. C. Dix", "Old English.", page 32.
alt.es: Tabla impresa con el encabezado "INDEX. First Series.", con columnas de número, título, fuente de la letra, melodía y página, que enumera veinte villancicos del I al XX. La fila XIV dice "What Child is this?", "W. C. Dix", "Old English.", página 32.

caption.en: The index of the first series of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old (first published 1867), in a later, undated printing: it gives the words of No. XIV to W. C. Dix and the air as Old English, and names no one for the harmony.
caption.es: El índice de la primera serie de Christmas Carols New and Old de Bramley y Stainer (publicada por primera vez en 1867), en una impresión posterior sin fecha: atribuye la letra del n.º XIV a W. C. Dix y la melodía a "Old English", y no nombra a nadie por la armonía.

source: H. R. Bramley and John Stainer, Christmas Carols New and Old, first series (London: Novello, Ewer and Co., undated, [187?]), "Index. First Series" (printed sideways; shown turned upright)
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London, undated: the Internet Archive catalogues it [187?]; the imprint is Novello, Ewer and Co. (the firm's name until 1898). John Stainer 1840-1901, Henry Ramsden Bramley 1833-1916, William Chatterton Dix 1837-1898 (Internet Archive record, which marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of a printed page of advertisements headed "The Musical Times. December 1, 1867." and numbered 235. In the left column, under "Christmas Carols, Old and New" in black-letter type, a numbered list of twenty carols with their composers; number 14 reads "What Child is this?" and "Old English." The right column advertises other Christmas anthems and carols.
alt.es: La parte superior de una página impresa de anuncios, con el encabezado "The Musical Times. December 1, 1867." y el número 235. En la columna izquierda, bajo "Christmas Carols, Old and New" en letra gótica, una lista numerada de veinte villancicos con sus compositores; el número 14 dice "What Child is this?" y "Old English." La columna derecha anuncia otros himnos y villancicos de Navidad.

caption.en: Novello's advertisement in the Musical Times of 1 December 1867, page 235, listing all twenty carols of Bramley and Stainer's book, which the same issue lists among Novello's publications of the past month: No. 14 is What Child is this?, its music Old English.
caption.es: El anuncio de Novello en el Musical Times del 1 de diciembre de 1867, página 235, con los veinte villancicos del libro de Bramley y Stainer, que el mismo número incluye entre las publicaciones de Novello del último mes: el n.º 14 es What Child is this?, con música "Old English".

source: The Musical Times, vol. 13, no. 298 (London: Novello, 1 December 1867), p. 235, advertisement "Christmas Carols. Old and New." (detail: the top half of the page)
licenceEvidence: Published London, 1 December 1867, as an unsigned publisher's advertisement; the people it names died by 1916 (Stainer 1901, Bramley 1916). PD by age in the US, the EU and Israel. Faithful microfilm scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: The Musical Times, 1 December 1867, via the Internet Archive
